clue.text: Eternal punishment of mother country

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: A grim complaint about the endless suffering the mother country inflicts on its people.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is the theological condemnation of a soul to everlasting torment in hell.

clue.text: Closed part of hospital promoted by head of neurology

indicators.note: in a down clue, being promoted means moving upwards, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a ward is a section of a hospital

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of neurology

explanation.surface: A hospital department closes, while a neurology chief gets a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains that are drawn are pulled shut, so drawn can mean closed.

clue.text: Short time with loose Canadian cop

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a brief while
to loose is to untie, as a verb

explanation.surface: A Canadian police officer briefly let off the leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, the national police force.

clue.text: Encourage sailor on film

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the standard abbreviation for a sailor
E.T. is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: Cheering on a sailor who appears in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the sailor sits on top of the film.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to support or urge someone on, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Chilled journalist following immoral capitalist leaders

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the journalist is placed second although the clue names it first
leaders are the front runners, so each word gives up only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of immoral and capitalist
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter left cold while trailing after unscrupulous business bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iced has been cooled with ice, so it is chilled.

clue.text: Lowest trap catching vacuum flask

indicators.note: a trap catching something holds it inside, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a net is a trap for fish or birds
Thermos is the brand name used generically for a vacuum flask

explanation.surface: A miserable trap that has snared someone's flask.
explanation.walkthrough: Thermos is a trademark that has become the everyday British word for any vacuum flask.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost is an old-fashioned superlative meaning furthest down, the very bottom.

clue.text: Glue crown around sovereign's head

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps itself about the other

parts.note: the pate is the crown of the head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is all that is used

parts.note: the first letter of sovereign

explanation.surface: Fixing a crown onto a monarch's head with adhesive.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown misleads towards royalty with sovereign; here it is the top of the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a soft adhesive, as in wallpaper paste, so it is a kind of glue.

clue.text: Punches salesperson upset by Foreign Office charges

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office
rates are charges or fees

explanation.surface: A salesman, angered by government fees, lashes out with his fists.
explanation.walkthrough: Punches reads as a violent noun; it is the verb for making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To perforate is to pierce holes through something, as a hole punch does to paper.

clue.text: Mark crosses river that is more terrifying

indicators.note: a pair that crosses something spans it from one side to the other, so it sits outside

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
R is the abbreviation for river
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A scar stretching across a river sounds like something out of a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: The mark and the river together straddle the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarier is the comparative of scary, meaning causing more fear.

clue.text: Appear caught in New York crisis

parts.note: to emerge is to come into view

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone shows up trapped in a New York emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden dangerous situation needing urgent action, which is a crisis.

clue.text: Unruly amateurs menaced gaming venue

indicators.note: unruly means out of control, so the letters do not keep their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Rowdy novices threatened people at a place full of games.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a hall of coin-operated slot and video machines, a gaming venue.

clue.text: Letter isn't vowel?

parts.note: isn't contains the negative not
E is one of the vowels

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a certain letter of the alphabet counts as a vowel.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter seems to be an alphabet character; it is a short written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a brief written message, a short letter.

clue.text: Attractive person embracing firm master

indicators.note: embracing means holding in one's arms, so one word wraps round the others

parts.note: a being is a living person or creature
CO is the abbreviation for company
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A good-looking type hugging the boss of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that is becoming flatters the wearer, so it looks attractive.

clue.text: Axe cut by strange old peasant

indicators.note: strange means odd or abnormal, so the letters are disordered
something cut by another thing has that thing driven into its middle

parts.note: a chopper is an axe
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An old farm labourer wounded by a strange axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy rustic, a country bumpkin who stomps through clods of earth.

clue.text: German rye breads baked for old men

indicators.note: baking transforms dough, so the letters are reformed into a new order

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: German rye loaves made for the elderly gentlemen of the village.
explanation.definitionFit: Greybeards are elderly men, named for their grey beards.

clue.text: Engineer melds true instrument

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the letters are built into something new

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer welds together a precise musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Engineer looks like a person; it is a verb telling you to rebuild the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel drum, or steelpan, is a Caribbean percussion instrument made from an oil drum.

clue.text: Thing returned by Carpathian in cry for help now and then

indicators.note: in puts the preceding pieces inside the following word

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an item is a thing
the setter Carpathian refers to themself, giving me

explanation.surface: The setter sends back something in a desperate call for rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpathian is the setter's pseudonym, so it stands for me.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometimes means occasionally, on some occasions but not always.

clue.text: Article about professional protective wear

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A news piece on what a professional wears for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: Article suggests a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a garment worn over clothes to keep them clean, a piece of protective clothing.

clue.text: Small motorbike moved aimlessly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a low-powered motorcycle with pedals
second meaning: past tense of mope, to wander listlessly

explanation.surface: A little motorcycle drifting about with no destination.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a light motorcycle and the past tense of mope, to drift about gloomily.

clue.text: Friend covers artist thus in shade

indicators.note: to cover something is to enclose it, so one word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a pal is a friend
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
so means thus

explanation.surface: A friend shelters a painter, keeping them out of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella giving shade from the sun, so it is a kind of sunshade.

clue.text: Starry eyed about dropping right song

indicators.note: about means all around, suggesting the letters are turned every which way
dropping means letting go, and right is the R abbreviation, so one such letter goes

parts.note: the letters to be used, less one

explanation.surface: Dreamy fans growing misty-eyed over a favourite number.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one of the two Rs, then rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday is the much-covered Beatles song by Paul McCartney.

clue.text: Fan voted out by heads of electronic engineering

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters are put out of sequence

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heads are the tops, so only each word's first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letters of electronic and engineering

explanation.surface: An enthusiast thrown out by a vote of the engineering department heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee is an ardent follower or enthusiast, which is what a fan is.

clue.text: Twist on top of pie

parts.note: a twist is a turn
over means on top of

explanation.surface: A cook adding a twist of decoration to the crust of a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a small pie made by folding pastry over a filling, such as an apple turnover.

clue.text: Egg on valiant ultra marathoners at the start

indicators.note: at the start points to the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Cheering on brave long-distance runners as the race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg looks like an urging verb, as in egg on; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovum is a female reproductive cell, the biological egg.

clue.text: Dirty setter's embracing posh Doctor of Divinity

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: the setter's things are my things
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
DD is the degree abbreviation for Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A grubby crossword compiler hugs an upper-crust clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddy means covered in mud, so it is dirty.

clue.text: Knocks over box

indicators.note: over can mean turned over, so the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: raps are knocks

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a box.
explanation.walkthrough: Box looks like a container; it is the verb to fight with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice or in a light exchange of punches.

clue.text: Part of body overcome by chemical imbalance

indicators.note: overcome by means swallowed up by, so the answer is enclosed within the next words

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A bodily organ affected by a chemical imbalance.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is an arm or leg, a part of the body.

clue.text: Roughly appraised import as stolen

indicators.note: roughly means carelessly or crudely, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A customs officer valued an imported item loosely, suspecting it was stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Misappropriated means taken dishonestly for one's own use, which is stolen.

clue.text: Fly across lake powered by the sun

indicators.note: flying across something spans it, so one word straddles the other

parts.note: to soar is to fly high
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An aircraft crossing a lake on sunlight alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means relating to or drawing energy from the sun, as in solar panels.

clue.text: Where plants grow is quiet and springy

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
rubbery means elastic, springy

explanation.surface: A garden described as peaceful with soft, bouncy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is an area planted with shrubs, a place where bushes grow.
